summary: Every running program is a process. You can start a command in the background with &, list your jobs, and stop one with kill.
notes: In your own terminal, sleep 30 & also prints a line like [1] 4821: the job number and the process ID (PID). PIDs change every run, so this page hides them.
kill %1 uses the job number. kill 4821 uses a PID, which you can find with ps or pgrep sleep.
Press Ctrl+C to stop a command running in the foreground, and fg to bring a background job back to the front.
pitfall: kill 1 without the % sends the signal to process ID 1, not job 1, and fails with kill: (1) - Operation not permitted. Write kill %1 for a job number.
